department: Department of Materials Science and Engineering

deadline.value: January 1 recommended deadline for Fall admission
deadline.quote: For both M.S. and Ph.D. applications, we strongly recommend submitting your application no later than January 1st for Fall semester admission and August 1st for Spring semester admission. Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis until all openings are filled or the admission deadline set forth by the Graduate School has been met.

gre_general.value: The GRE is not required by the College of Engineering.
gre_general.quote: The GRE subject test is no longer required by our school—neither the General Test nor any Subject Test.

gre_subject.value: ETS offers no Materials subject test.
gre_subject.quote: The GRE Subject Tests in Mathematics, Physics and Psychology measure undergraduate achievement in a particular field of study

supervisor.value: Students are paired with a faculty advisor upon acceptance based on research interests.
supervisor.quote: Upon acceptance, students are paired with a faculty advisor based on their research interests, and meetings with advisors typically occur on a regular basis to ensure continuous progress.

funding.value: All Ph.D. students receive financial aid through assistantships with full tuition coverage and stipends.
funding.quote: The UConn College of Engineering offers competitive financial support for Ph.D. students, including stipends, full tuition coverage, and health insurance. | All Ph.D. students receive financial aid through research assistantships (RAs) or teaching assistantships (TAs), which provide a stipend based on the assistantship type and department.

entry_route.value: Direct admission to Ph.D. program without an MS degree is permitted.
entry_route.quote: Can I apply directly to the Ph.D. Program without an MS degree? | Yes.
